issues.description: The Ride.name attribute is declared public in the solution (public String name;) but the UML in the problem statement uses '-' (private) for the Ride attributes and the exercise instructions ask students to create attributes and provide getters. This visibility mismatch (public vs. private expected by UML) can confuse students about the intended encapsulation and how to implement the class and its getters.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Ride.name attribute private (private String name;) in the solution to match the UML's private visibility and the exercise instructions, and keep the public getter getName(). Alternatively, if public visibility was intentional, update the UML and problem statement to reflect a public attribute.
